title: Software
description: Types for building and shipping software.

types.title: Application
types.description: A software application the work uses or targets, such as a CAD program or a browser.

types.title: Feature
types.description: A capability of a product. Built means merged but not yet in a release.

order.description: Position on the roadmap among its siblings. Lower comes first.

tokens_estimated.description: How many tokens an agent expects this to take in all: input and output, not counting cached re-reads. It stands only while none of the tasks that are part of it has an estimate: after that the feature is the sum of its tasks.

tokens_used.description: Tokens spent on it directly, measured from the sessions that worked on it. What its tasks used is added when it is shown.

types.title: Proof
types.description: Something a user would ask before trusting the software, such as how we know the sun is correct. The title is the question. It is answered on a build when every test of it passed there: that is worked out from the results, not stored.

types.title: Test
types.description: One check that helps answer a proof question. A draft is a test that is wanted and not yet written. What it found is kept per build, as test results.

compares.description: What is compared with what, in one line a user can read: the position of the sun against the NOAA calculator in six cities.

tolerance.description: How close it must be to pass, e.g. within 0.01 degrees.

environment.description: Where it runs and draws its picture: outside any host, or inside the program it extends.

types.title: Test result
types.description: What one test found on one build. There is one for each test on each build; a later run on the same build replaces it.

evidence.description: Where the proof is: a path, URL or commit.

build.description: The version or commit the test ran on.

picture.description: Where the picture the test drew is: a path in the repository it ran in, under its .proof folder, which git ignores. The file itself is sent to Archipelago (picture_put) only when the result is shown in public.

types.title: Environment
types.description: Somewhere software runs: a machine, a VM, staging, production.

types.title: Component
types.description: A part of a running system: a service, a store, a proxy, a model endpoint, a client. Part of the environment it runs in; it calls (software.calls) what it sends to, the link's says naming how (HTTPS, SQL) and its state saying whether it is wired, planned or broken. Its status is its health, kept true as it is wired up and watched: standby is built but stopped on purpose (the idle colour of a blue-green pair), which monitors leave alone. Drawn by the architecture shape.

role.description: What it does in the system. data and storage are drawn as a cylinder, client as a pill.

layer.description: What it is, in a system of a kernel and packs: the kernel, a pack of types (a workspace's), a pack the whole server runs, a store, a service outside, or yours (your browser, your agents). A style may colour a part's dot by it (dots).

host.description: Where it runs, as its operator names it: a container, a machine, a region.

url.description: The address its health is read from: what its monitor checks (http(s)://…, or tcp://host:port for a port). A monitor reporting on it moves the status between up and down.

commit.description: The commit it runs, as its deploy last reported.

types.title: Handoff
types.description: Where a working session left things for the next one.

note_max.say: It holds one of each part (not seen working, what bites here, next and why). Rewrite it whole with body: keep what is still so, drop what later work settled, and put what is true of one item in that item's note.

types.title: Diagram
types.description: One page of a diagram made from the code (npm run diagrams), kept as data its page draws: boxes, areas and the wires between them, at the commit it was made from.

diagram.description: The page as data: its boxes with where each is, its wires, the draw.io file and page it is (key), the commit it was drawn from, and that file at the commit (drawio) when it was committed as drawn.

actions.title: Report a test run
actions.description: Say what a test run found on one build. Each result names its test by id or by its entrypoint (the name the harness knows it by) and says whether it passed, with the measured value, where the evidence is and the picture the test drew. One result is kept per test per build: reported again, it is replaced, and the pictures kept for that test's results are removed. Where a test answers a public question, the answer names the pictures to send now (answer.send_pictures: each with picture_put). A test the map does not know is named in the answer (answer.unknown) and nothing is made for it: create the software.test first and link it to the proof question it helps answer. Called as test_report.

build.description: The version or commit the tests ran on.

test.description: The test: its id, or its entrypoint.

value.description: The headline number or outcome, e.g. "0.004 degrees".

evidence.description: Where the proof is: a path, URL or commit.

picture.description: Where the picture the test drew is: a path in the repository, under its .proof folder (which git ignores), e.g. ".proof/1.0.0/Sun.MatchesNoaa.png". The file is not sent here.

link.description: Where the run can be looked at.

views.description: Where a repository's work stands, for the session picking it up: the last push, the handoff note (the part an agent wrote: what the map cannot know), what has happened since that note was written (pushes, what was settled, what was opened, the sessions that ended and what each said), and the open work, ready and blocked. Read this first. Params: repo (required): its id, GitHub name or title; since (an ISO date-time to count from, instead of when the note was written).

repo.description: The repository: its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

since.description: An ISO date-time to count from, instead of when the note was written.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: Open tasks, decisions and issues belonging to whatever lives in a repository, split into ready and blocked, and when GitHub last reported a push to it. Params: repo (required): its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

repo.description: The repository: its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: What is due for a scheduled re-check in a repository: each project living there says how often its oldest items are re-checked (its recheck_days; weekly when not set, 0 for never; a feature living there on its own takes its project's), and for each that has waited that long (waited), its open items nobody has changed or confirmed in that time, oldest first, leaving out what waits on a person. Params: repo (required): its id, GitHub name or title, limit (items per project, default 25), now (true to be given the oldest items of every project there, whatever its interval and however new they are).

repo.description: The repository: its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

now.description: true for the oldest items of every project there, whatever its interval.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: How we know the software is correct: the proof questions of a product (a project or feature; a question is a software.proof that is part of it or about it), each with the tests that help answer it and what every test found on one build, with its picture. A question is answered on a build when all its tests passed there. Params: of (an entity id; without it, the projects that have proof questions), build (a version or commit; without it, the build last reported).

of.description: A project or feature; without it, the projects that have proof questions.

build.description: A version or commit; without it, the build last reported.

within.description: In place of of: only these items and what is part of them (a gate's stake, a public page's items).

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: What a product has to show: its features that are built or shipped, each with the release it went out in; built and not yet released first, then the newest. Planned work is not in it. Params: of (required): a project or feature.

within.description: Only these items, as a public page gives them.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

views.description: What agents have used in a repository: each run there that counted its tokens (a session on a machine, the sync agent in GitHub Actions), newest first, and the sum by where they ran over the last 7 and 30 days. Params: repo (required): its id, GitHub name or title; limit (runs listed, default 20).

repo.description: The repository: its id, its GitHub name "owner/name", or its title.

full.description: true for the answer whole, as the screen has it.

relations.title: lives in
relations.description: The repository that holds the work.

relations.title: uses
relations.description: An application the work depends on or targets.

relations.title: helps answer
relations.description: The test is part of how we know. A proof question is answered on a build when every test that helps answer it passed there.

relations.title: calls
relations.description: A wire of a running system: the one part sends to the other (a request, a query, a backup). It blocks nothing. props.says names how (HTTPS, SQL); props.state is wired, planned or broken, and left out it is read from the health of the two ends.

trees.title: Roadmap
trees.description: A project's features in the order they are to be built, the work under each, and where work is happening now.
